beats.headline: Caretakers of the upside-down castle
beats.text: From a crawler's note in the Cookbook, written in awe: Larracos is an inverted funnel of museums, galleries and colleges, too beautiful to be used this way. The Semeru dwarves supposedly built it, but they do not control it any more. They are still around, mostly in the pubs, and they are the non-combatant caretakers of the inverted castle at the bottom of the well. The author reads the city as a tower to the gods turned upside down: the Semeru dug toward the Celestials below them, and something at the base of the volcano woke.

beats.headline: Where the idea came from
beats.text: Clint has a theory about the nine-tier attack that blames the high elves. Crawler Carl has heard a different one, from the Cookbook: the Semeru dwarves of the ninth floor dug their city too deep, a Tower of Babel run in reverse. It was that story that gave Carl the idea to fill it with water in the first place.

beats.headline: Everything they had worked for
beats.text: The System, introducing Big Tina, runs down who paid for the nine-tier attack. The Over City was devastated. The residents of the Hunting Grounds were transmuted, all but the high elves. And the Semeru dwarves of Larracos lost everything they had been working for. Even the celestials, and their downstairs neighbours in Sheol, found their destinies altered that day. It is a list. The Semeru get one line of it.

beats.headline: Feeding the pit
beats.text: On Odette's show, Donut is appalled: Larracos has been flooded since the end of the fifth floor, and the sharks are still there. They get fed, says Odette. The Semeru are not letting anyone near that part of the city, and they are keeping the castle submerged. Mercenaries and players alike are going into that pit daily. The trouble at the Desperado Club ejected several officials and participants into it, all of them devoured or pulling their fail-safes. One of the dead was a warlord.

beats.headline: One goddess, one temple
beats.text: Another note from the Cookbook, this one by Crawler Allister. The Semeru dwarves of the ninth floor all worship a single goddess, who appears near the end of the battles as the last teams approach the gates of the castle of Larracos. She has one temple in the whole dungeon, and the author has never heard of a crawler worshipping her. The dwarves call her the Downward Spiral. Some say she is behind Scolopendra's nine-tier attack. Outside Larracos she has another name: the Vinegar Bitch.

beats.headline: The Warden opens the drain
beats.text: In a muddy alley of Larracos lies a long, jet-black concierge shark, level 41, not long dead. The System gives the cause: suffocation, when the Semeru Warden finally decided to open the drain. Crawler Carl throws it in the air and punches it with Daughter's Kiss. The shark vaporises, and Carl and Donut both go sliding through the mud.

beats.headline: Down to the roots
beats.text: The System gives the history. The Semeru once lived in peace in this fertile volcanic level, farming, mining, learning, and loving their goddess, Ysalte. They dug to reach her; a city of scholars grew in the pit. What they found were roots of the All Tree, which connects everything, and there they stopped, and built their castle along the roots as a monument and an apology. The nine-tier attack still hit them hardest. Millions before; fewer than ten thousand after. The city itself was untouched, and the survivors became its stewards.

beats.headline: No longer only caretakers
beats.text: Everything Crawler Carl had heard made the Semeru a drunk, defeated people who kept the castle clean and rarely fought their invaders. Not now. On a balcony a dwarf is teaching a boy to stab with a sword. Their war leader arrives in parade armour with a sickle, calls the crawlers Honored Warlords, and carries a Despondent debuff for his dead goddess. Donut asks in chat whether they know who flooded the city, and who killed the goddess. Carl tells her not to bring it up.

beats.headline: Singing on the down ramps
beats.text: The lower the tour goes, the busier Larracos gets. A squad of dwarves jogs past singing a military running cadence, hammers and sickles on their shoulders. The down ramps are mined, the flooded castle kept underwater by choice, and the NPC raids have reached the inner circle of every enemy camp but the nagas'. Most of them know about their past seasons; for most of them, one death is forever.

beats.headline: On the lip of the city
beats.text: Juice Box, stingy with support until now, lends ground troops to hold Shanty Town: mostly Semeru dwarves and ordinary citizens of Larracos, mixed in with Li Na's 107th White Dragon Urban Defense battalion in a ring around the lip of the city. During a bombing run, Britney's report reaches Louis in his cockpit: the Semeru are on standby, waiting for his bomb run.

beats.headline: Holding the college gate
beats.text: At the college gate, a line of Semeru dwarves in ornate parade armour holds back a surge of shadowy zarogoths. An orange ray from one of the mobs drops a dwarf onto his back, and the mob laughs. Another Semeru slashes its bulbous stomach open; it deflates in a gush of black liquid, dead, and the fallen dwarf writhes in the oil. A magic missile from Donut's tower lands among the ghouls, and the dwarves press the attack.

beats.headline: Putting the statue back
beats.text: The castle the Semeru built as a capstone against further intrusion toward the gods is wrecked: the living wood rotted away, the gem-inlaid stone barely holding a shape. A pair of Semeru stand on the shoulder of the idle dwarven digger, working a control panel. Afterwards, while soldiers and former crawlers repair towers and clear streets, a group of Semeru gather the pieces of the statue from the front of the castle and try to fit them back together.

beats.headline: With the city, to the Ascendency
beats.text: Closing arrangements for the ninth floor. The hired mercenaries are expected to vanish. The changelings, the thousands of NPCs who live in Larracos, and the Semeru dwarves are to move with the city to the Ascendency, where it is meant to land on a green hill above miles of cotton fields. The NPCs are untouchable there until the Ascendency begins. It is not safe. It is life.
